summary.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 43.4% YoY to INR426 crores, with same-store sales growth of 28.7% and pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin of 8.1%.
summary.overview: United Foodbrands (Barbeque Nation) reported its strongest quarter in recent years, with revenue of INR426 crores (+43.4% YoY), SSSG of 28.7% on top of 14.4% in Q4 FY26, and dine-in transactions up 63.5%. Growth was volume-led with no price increase taken, and value-led dayparts, Big Buffet and captive digital channels drove traffic. Pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 8.1% from about 5.5% in Q4 and about 350 bps YoY, helped by gross margin recovery in India and back-end cost leverage. Management guided that reported growth rates will moderate in H2 as comparables tighten, and held the 300-restaurant FY27 target.

segments.name: Barbeque Nation India
segments.commentary: SSSG 33.5%, revenue growth 43.4%, dine-in transactions +68.6%; India gross margin improved ~130 bps QoQ. Captive digital ecosystem contributed 65% of dine-in transactions (from ~61% in Q4); MAU ~1.4 million (+~60% YoY).

segments.name: Barbeque Nation International
segments.commentary: Revenue +46.6% YoY, SSSG 8.5%, dine-in volume +45.2%, gross profit +40.3%. Gross margin down ~3 pp on Middle East-linked inflation; one new UAE restaurant added.

segments.name: Premium CDR
segments.commentary: Revenue +~36%, SSSG 13.6%, dine-in volume +~40%. Added 1 and closed 1 restaurant, ending with the same network count; Q4 FY26 cohort maturing through FY27.

guidance_outlook: SSSG expected to moderate through FY27 as comparables tighten; Q3 and Q4 FY27 lap the strongest quarter of FY26. Management called this mathematical rather than a demand change.
Committed to reaching 300 restaurants by FY27 (266 at end Q1 after 5 additions); 15 restaurants under construction to open in Q2 and Q3 FY27; FY27 additions expected at ~40 versus ~35 in FY26.
FY27 capex guided at ~INR140 crores: ~INR120 crores for new outlets and ~INR20 crores for maintenance and ancillary capex.

Margin levers cited for FY27: India gross margin recovery, mature portfolio ROM expansion, new-store cohort maturation, and back-end cost leverage. No explicit double-digit EBITDA margin target given.
Continued funding of expansion mainly from internal accruals; borrowings to be kept at prudent levels.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 closed with 266 restaurants after 5 additions in the quarter (Barbeque Nation India portfolio ~210 restaurants).
15 restaurants under construction, operationalising in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
Management sees Barbeque Nation India able to reach ~600 restaurants on Big Buffet model across Tier 1-3 markets (up from earlier 400-450 view).
Format change: new restaurants at ~3,500 sq ft versus earlier ~4,500 sq ft; revenue per restaurant still among highest.
FY27 capex ~INR140 crores (INR120 crores new outlets, INR20 crores maintenance and ancillary).
demand_pricing: No price increase taken in Q1 FY27; growth entirely volume-led. Average price points declined due to value initiatives and have now stabilised.
Average revenue per mature restaurant rose to ~INR7 crores; management said the INR425 crore quarter exceeded the initial INR400 crore expectation and momentum continued into July.
Repeat customers ~45-47% of business; mix shifting slightly toward new customers. Average mature market covers ~7.1 pax per bill vs ~6.5 for BBQ India.
Delivery growth of 62% YoY supported by value SKUs across three brands (Barbeque Nation, BBQ, Dum Safar); delivery share up ~2 pp YoY, carrying commissions and packaging costs.
Management flagged inflation in UAE commodities of 30-40% in some cases; service-quality blip in April 2026 from manpower shortage, with guest scores improving over the last three months.

qa_highlights.question: How much more market does Big Buffet open up in Tier 2-4 towns, versus two years ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Big Buffet model, tested for about 6 quarters, can take Barbeque Nation India to around 600 restaurants at current scale, up from the earlier 400-450 view. It is working in towns with populations as low as 3 lakh and in cities where the first restaurant performs profitably.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the SSSG improvement, by brand?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-led volume strategy started in Barbeque Nation India and extended to International and Premium CDR. Marketing spend rose about 1 pp of revenue, and digital conversion improved. Average revenue per mature restaurant reached about INR7 crores, and management said momentum continued.

qa_highlights.question: Why is mature restaurant margin (16.2%) below the roughly 20% implied by flow-through, and is 18% a cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 3 pp from lower gross margin (about 2 pp) and higher marketing (about 1 pp), about 60 bps from delivery mix, and about 140-150 bps from energy, manpower and other inflation. It said it does not see 18% as a cap and that some of these factors are being worked on.

qa_highlights.question: Path to double-digit pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a target and said it is tracking levers: gross margin recovery, mature portfolio ROM, new-store cohort maturity and back-end leverage. It said the margin will be an outcome of these levers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised gross margin outlook and how will mix affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current 66-67% gross margin is a good operating band and expects directional movement from there. It attributed part of the gap to deliberate value investments and to faster-growing India mix, which is at a lower gross margin, and said the mix effect is not a concern while each segment grows.

qa_highlights.question: Repeat customer share and whether the SSSG was one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Repeat customers are about 45-47% of business, with the mix shifting slightly toward new guests. Management would not call the SSSG one-off. It said SSSG was negative until Q1 FY26, then about 8% in Q3, 14.5% in Q4 and 28% in Q1 FY27, and that UAE inflation is real, with gross margin down about 3 pp.

risks_watch: SSSG moderation in Q3 and Q4 FY27 as the strongest FY26 quarter is lapped; management framed it as mathematical, not demand-driven.
Input inflation in the UAE (commodity prices up 30-40% in some cases) and the Middle East situation weighing on International gross margin and restaurant margin, which was softer than typical in Q1.
Mature portfolio margin of 16.2% versus the roughly 20% management implied on flow-through; gross margin, marketing and energy/manpower inflation are still weighing on it.
Service quality: an April 2026 manpower shortage caused a blip; guest scores have improved over the last three months, but management acknowledged possible service strain at higher volumes.
Delivery growth of 62% carries commissions and packaging costs, which dilute flow-through; management did not disclose delivery profitability.
Expansion pace: 15 restaurants due in Q2-Q3 FY27 and about 40 FY27 additions needed to reach 300; net debt rose to INR106 crores and FY27 capex is about INR140 crores.
key_quotes: This has been our strongest operating quarter in recent years with multiple performance benchmarks being achieved simultaneously.
We view this as a mathematical consequence of stronger comparatives rather than any change in underlying consumer demand.
I think the current levels of around 66% -67% range is a good operating band and we would expect to move directionally from here over time.
And rather than chasing a number, I think we should look at what are the margin levers and are we moving in the right direction.
summary.management_tone: Confident and volume-focused on the quarter, with repeated caution on the outlook: management said SSSG will moderate through FY27 and declined to give a SSSG number, a double-digit EBITDA margin target or a one-off view. It was candid on International and UAE inflation and on the mature-margin gap, and deflected on the video and food-quality complaint.
